messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Favicon displays locally but not on shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Favicon displays locally but not on shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Greg,

This is fallout from a change we made a few weeks ago where applications are now hosted inside an iframe. The purpose of this change was to support custom domains (as well as lay the ground work for some future changes we would like to build).

I am afraid that with this change the domain for your application (account.shinyapps.io/app <http://account.shinyapps.io/app>) is not actually your application, rather its a dynamic page that serves an iframe that embeds your application. Your application is now served from a URL (internal.shinyapps.io/account/app <http://internal.shinyapps.io/account/app>). I am not sure if any workaround exists right now that will enable the use of favicons, but it is something we can look at addressing in a future release.

I am sorry, and I wish I had better news.
-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] evaluating shinyapps.io - bioinformatics data heavy apps
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] evaluating shinyapps.io - bioinformatics data heavy apps
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

See my responses inline.

On Tue, Jun 30, 2015 at 2:36 PM, Abhishek Pratap <abhish...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hey Guys
>
> We are currently evaluating using shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> for deploying some of our production apps (bioinformatics based). For our implementation we have few requirements.
>
> 1. we need to be able to connect to our server to fetch data in real time. This means we need to be able to store username/passwd information

Sure. Many people like to store their username / passwords in a .Rprofile which is included in the app when deploying.

> 2. download data from our server to shinyapps server

Obviously this is dependent on how you are downloaded the data, but as long as the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers have access this should be fine. Keep in mind however, that data downloaded will not be saved after re-deploying the application (all data written to a shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> application instance is ephemeral). So downloaded large amounts of data may result in performance issues. Read more here <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html#application-instances>.

> 3. install R/Python libs for code dependencies

This may be an issue. Installing most R packages is supported, and even custom packages hosted on GitHub. However python packages may not be supported. shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> doesn't currently support installing arbitrary python packages at this time. This is something we've discussed adding, but have no immediate plans at thsi time. It may be possible to port your python code to R.

>
> Just wondering if RStudio folks or community have addressed similar issues before.
>
> Best,
> -Abhi

messages.subject: Can't deploy app to shinyapps because "suggested" packages don't get installed
messages.subject_clean: Can't deploy app to shinyapps because "suggested" packages don't get installed
messages.body_plain:
My package `shinyjs` has a single function `shinyjs::extendShinyjs()` that relies on the package `V8`.  Since it's a fairly advanced function, I didn't want to put `V8` in the "imports" section of the package, and instead it's in the "suggests" section, because I don't want to force everyone to download the V8 package since most users will never need it.

Deploying an app that uses `shinyjs::extendShinyjs()` results in an error on shinyapps since the `V8` package doesn't get installed.  The user has to make a call to `library(V8)` in order for the app to work, but that's a bit awkward because the user never makes any function calls using V8.

I'm not sure what the correct behaviour here would be - does it make sense to install suggested packages? Am I doing it wrong with my package shinyjs, and I should be including V8 in "imports"?

messages.subject: Store Data Beyond Application Instances
messages.subject_clean: Store Data Beyond Application Instances
messages.body_plain:
I read that data written by an application to the local filesystem of an instance will be lost when the app is re-deployed. The application I'm writing allows users to submit some new data to the application and compare it to the existing data. The new data should be saved with the existing data, so that the dataset can grow as users make submissions and remain in the dataset if the server is restarted. It's basically a data frame that grows when users submit new results. What alternative method is there to achieve this ?

Also, the webpage <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html#application-instances> states "By default, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> deploys all applications on ‘medium’ instances", but the table below has small instances shown as the default.

messages.body_plain:
I don't think it makes much sense for you to import V8 in your package
if you do not really rely on it for most of your functions to work. In
this particular case, the question is how to tell shinyapps that V8 is
really needed even if it is in Suggests. Suggests is kind of a "gray"
area: you may or may not need these packages. There are pros and cons
of forcing to install all suggested packages, but I feel the solution
is trivial enough in this case so we probably don't want to think too
hard which option is the "correct" one :)

Regards,
Yihui

We don't have such a feature, but it is a good one to add to our list.  We have been thinking about auditing for RStudio Server Pro and Shiny Server Pro, but we hadn't talked about it for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>
I will add it to our backlog, and probably reach out to you to talk about what are the types of actions you would want to see in the logs.  A shiny application could literally have thousands of events during the course of someone interacting with the application so thinking through what would be useful to keep is hard.
-Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Can't deploy app to shinyapps because "suggested" packages don't get installed
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Can't deploy app to shinyapps because "suggested" packages don't get installed
messages.body_plain:
Dean et al.,

When shinyapps does dependency detection on an app, it does not include suggested packages. The reason for this is that dependency detection is recursive, and when we did our initial testing of including suggested packages, even relatively simple applications ended up having hundreds of dependencies. Additionally, many times suggested packages are suggested because they are burdensome to install or have non-trivial system dependancies which may or may not work on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.

However, this is not to say that our current approach is ideal for exactly the reasons you've outlined. We could look at some alternate approaches. Some ideas:

1) Right now our dependency detection code is unsophisticated in that it requires that all detected dependencies (e.g. Depends, Imports, LinkingTo) be installed. Including suggested packages results in the explosion of packages I mentioned above.

An alternate approach may be to only include suggested packages if they are actually installed on the end-user's system. For example: if an app depends on shinyjs and V8 is suggested by shinyjs, if the user has the V8 package installed locally we will include it (and its recursive dependencies). Conversely, if the package rJava was suggested, but not installed locally we wont include it.

This approach may or not be better for a number of reasons. I did some testing and in my opinion we still end up with lots of packages still being installed unnecessarily (many user's end up with lots of packages installed on their system over time, and packages often have many suggested packages that are not really related).

For example on my system I started with the simplest app possible; basically an application with just library(shiny).

Without suggested dependencies:

> appDependencies("../shinyapps-test/sessioninfo")

12 vs 58 is quite a jump despite the fact that I'm including only including suggested packages that I have installed.

Another variation could be to include suggested dependencies non-recursively. Basically this means that only directly detected dependancies (e.g. detected calls to require/library) will have their suggested dependencies installed. Here is the result of that:

> appDependencies("../shinyapps-test/sessioninfo")

Which is a little better, but 37 vs 12 is a lot. The reason for this is because shiny has 6 suggested dependencies, which themselves have lots of required dependencies (again this is for the simplest possible app).

This might be workable, but the distinction seems arbitrary in my mind. I like to avoid arbitrary distinctions as they tend to lead to more confusion in the end.

So my feeling is that this approach sounds great in theory, but in practice its still too many packages to install. Perhaps this option can be toggle-able via an option. But I feel like this may be useless in the end, because it still requires the end-user to know they need to set the option. In my experience nobody ever RTFM, so this is probably no better then documenting that the end user needs to do require(XXX) for suggested packages in their app when running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/>, as it still requires the user to do something.

You can checkout my code for this test here: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/compare/suggested-package-dependencies?expand=1

2) Another possibility is to allow package maintainers to use a special DESCRIPTION field to have custom dependencies for shinyapps:

For example we could look for a ShinyAppsDepends field in the DESCRIPTION file for a package:

ShinyAppsDepends: V8

If we see that, we can include it. This approach might be better, because only package maintainers would have to know about the workaround, rather then end-users.

Anyway, these are some ideas, and I am open to other suggestions as well.

-Andy

> 12 vs 58 is quite a jump despite the fact that I'm including only including suggested packages that I have installed.

> Another variation could be to include suggested dependencies non-recursively. Basically this means that only directly detected dependancies (e.g. detected calls to require/library) will have their suggested dependencies installed. Here is the result of that:

>

>

But I feel like this may be useless in the end, because it still requires the end-user to know they need to set the option. In my experience nobody ever RTFM, so this is probably no better then documenting that the end user needs to do require(XXX) for suggested packages in their app when running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/>, as it still requires the user to do something.

> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > If someone can provide a solution, obviously I'd like it to work with shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, so the local port binding would need to be one that is available on the service.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > I guess there are other convoluted options, like running the SQL query on the same machine as the database, saving results as a CSV and then making that CSV available to my shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> app. This is not ideal, because I'd like to write data back to the database too, and this ust seems like an intermediate step which is not really optimum.

> On Thursday, 21 May 2015 14:45:19 UTC+2, Tareef Kawaf wrote:
> > I am not 100% sure if this helps, but I know some people use security groups for this purpose as well.  From our FAQ.
> >
> > You’ll need to add RStudio’s EC2 Security Group to the database:
> > 1. Log into your Amazon AWS console
> > 2. Click on the RDS Dashboard under the Database section
> > 3. Navigate to the Security Groups tab
> > 4. Select the database you want to allow access to
> > 5. At the very bottom there is a dropdown for Connection Type, select EC2 Security Group
> > 6. Select Another Account
> > 7. Enter the account ID and Security Group name for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>:
> > AWS Account ID: 954555569365
> > EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
> > 8. Authorize!
> >

> > > Ok. Thanks Jack.
> > >
> > >
> > > On Saturday, May 16, 2015 at 1:06:04 AM UTC+10, ja...@prismfp.com wrote:
> > > > Tim,
> > > >
> > > > I may be wrong, but I have tried to do this with a VPC, and I have concluded that the only way is to allow access from the individual IP addresses mentioned in Chad Barraford's post above from 2 Feb.
> > > >
> > > > If you find out how to get it to work using ShinyApps.io's security group, then I would be pleased to hear about it. However it seems that in any case you would have to be in the same AWS geographic zone as the ShinyApps servers for this to work. IP addresses work anywhere.
> > > >
> > > > Jack
> > > >
> > > > On Friday, 8 May 2015 00:49:47 UTC+1, Tim Beveridge wrote:

> > > > >
> > > > > I'm wondering if you have any tips on setting the security in that environment so shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> can access it :-)
> > > > >
> > > > > Cheers,
> > > > >
> > > > > Tim
> > > > >
> > > > > On Thursday, May 7, 2015 at 7:27:08 AM UTC+10, Scott Shepard wrote:
> > > > > > Of course.
> > > > > >

> > > > > >       AWS Account ID: 954555569365
> > > > > >       EC2 Security Group Name: production-agents
> > > > > > 8. Authorize!
> > > > > >
> > > > > > And you're done. The shinyapps servers have access to your MySQL database without making system calls or setting up an ssh tunnel.

> > > > > > On Tuesday, May 5, 2015 at 12:54:29 PM UTC-5, Paolo Cavatore wrote:
> > > > > > > A Step-by-Step guide would be appreciated if possible...hopefully using Amazon RDS

> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > I've been trying to setup an auto-closing ssh tunnel with something like this:
> > > > > > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > > > > > I've been using ps aux | grep sshd to check the tunnel is created and then after 10 seconds of non-activity closes. This bit seems to work fine.
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > However, I'm still somewhat stuck when trying to execute my local MySQL query. The error is:
> > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > Error in .local(drv, ...) :
> > > > > > > > > > > >   Failed to connect to database: Error: Can't connect to MySQL server on 'hostname' (111)
> > > > > > > > > > > >

messages.body_plain:
Sometimes you can see whether your instance is running out of memory if you look at the javascript console.  I would update the instance size up to a higher size and see if you continue to have the issue you are seeing.   If you include a link to the application, it might be possible for us to see the issue through the javascript console.

Homer

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] billing when you exceed your plan's hour-limit
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] billing when you exceed your plan's hour-limit
messages.body_plain:
Homer,

Currently we do not change for overages on active hours. In the future, per the terms of our shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> terms of use, we will change a small overage fee on a per-hour basis for users who are over their subscription limit. We've not yet determined what that fee would be.

So you need not worry for the time being.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Can't deploy app to shinyapps because "suggested" packages don't get installed
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Can't deploy app to shinyapps because "suggested" packages don't get installed
messages.body_plain:
Is there any place to track the progress of issues/bugs with shinyapps? I'd like to know if/when this issue gets addressed

---
http://deanattali.com

On 2 July 2015 at 08:52, Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Andy - thanks for such a thoughtful response. I do agree with you on all the issues and that most of the solutions are not ideal, and arbitrary cutoffs are bad, etc.  I do like the last idea of adding a special field in DESCRIPTION for shinyapps, maybe that idea can be explored more in depth to see if it makes sense.
>
>
> On Thursday, 2 July 2015 08:41:48 UTC-7, Andy Kipp wrote:
> > Dean et al.,
> >
> > When shinyapps does dependency detection on an app, it does not include suggested packages. The reason for this is that dependency detection is recursive, and when we did our initial testing of including suggested packages, even relatively simple applications ended up having hundreds of dependencies. Additionally, many times suggested packages are suggested because they are burdensome to install or have non-trivial system dependancies which may or may not work on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
> >
> > However, this is not to say that our current approach is ideal for exactly the reasons you've outlined. We could look at some alternate approaches. Some ideas:
> >
> > 1) Right now our dependency detection code is unsophisticated in that it requires that all detected dependencies (e.g. Depends, Imports, LinkingTo) be installed. Including suggested packages results in the explosion of packages I mentioned above.
> >
> > An alternate approach may be to only include suggested packages if they are actually installed on the end-user's system. For example: if an app depends on shinyjs and V8 is suggested by shinyjs, if the user has the V8 package installed locally we will include it (and its recursive dependencies). Conversely, if the package rJava was suggested, but not installed locally we wont include it.
> >
> > This approach may or not be better for a number of reasons. I did some testing and in my opinion we still end up with lots of packages still being installed unnecessarily (many user's end up with lots of packages installed on their system over time, and packages often have many suggested packages that are not really related).
> >
> > For example on my system I started with the simplest app possible; basically an application with just library(shiny).
> >
> > Without suggested dependencies:
> >
> > > appDependencies("../shinyapps-test/sessioninfo")
> >      package version
> > 1      shiny  0.12.0

> >
> > Now I run again and include suggested packages (recursively) and their required dependencies.

> > 1         shiny   0.12.0
> > 2         utils    3.1.2

> > 12        tools    3.1.2
> > 13     datasets    3.1.2
> > 14        Cairo    1.5-5

> >
> > 12 vs 58 is quite a jump despite the fact that I'm including only including suggested packages that I have installed.
> >
> > Another variation could be to include suggested dependencies non-recursively. Basically this means that only directly detected dependancies (e.g. detected calls to require/library) will have their suggested dependencies installed. Here is the result of that:
> >
> > > appDependencies("../shinyapps-test/sessioninfo")

> > 11         Rcpp  0.11.2

> > 34    dichromat   2.0-0
> > 35      munsell   0.4.2
> > 36     labeling     0.2
> > 37   colorspace   1.2-4
> >
> > Which is a little better, but 37 vs 12 is a lot. The reason for this is because shiny has 6 suggested dependencies, which themselves have lots of required dependencies (again this is for the simplest possible app).
> >
> > This might be workable, but the distinction seems arbitrary in my mind. I like to avoid arbitrary distinctions as they tend to lead to more confusion in the end.
> >
> > So my feeling is that this approach sounds great in theory, but in practice its still too many packages to install. Perhaps this option can be toggle-able via an option. But I feel like this may be useless in the end, because it still requires the end-user to know they need to set the option. In my experience nobody ever RTFM, so this is probably no better then documenting that the end user needs to do require(XXX) for suggested packages in their app when running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/>, as it still requires the user to do something.
> >
> > You can checkout my code for this test here: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/compare/suggested-package-dependencies?expand=1
> >
> > 2) Another possibility is to allow package maintainers to use a special DESCRIPTION field to have custom dependencies for shinyapps:
> >
> > For example we could look for a ShinyAppsDepends field in the DESCRIPTION file for a package:
> >
> > ShinyAppsDepends: V8
> >
> > If we see that, we can include it. This approach might be better, because only package maintainers would have to know about the workaround, rather then end-users.
> >
> > Anyway, these are some ideas, and I am open to other suggestions as well.
> >
> > -Andy
> >
> > On Thu, Jul 2, 2015 at 5:42 AM, Tareef Kawaf <tar...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > > I think this is something that the shinyapps team has discussed in the past and I honestly can't remember why we didn't pick up the suggests.  I think it was mostly to avoid the bloat of loading up a ton of packages that may or may not be needed.
> > > Andy is probably the person that will need to comment on this :)
> > >
> > > -Tareef
> > >
> > > On Thu, Jul 2, 2015 at 8:39 AM, Dean Attali <daat...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Thanks Yihui, good to know I'm not alone in this thinking. I'm not sure who the shinyapps team is, but yes hopefully they give input about this

Teresa

messages.body_plain:
Hi, I am using R v3.1.2 and Rtools v3.2

I run my code the following way:

install.packages('devtools')
devtools::install_github('rstudio/shinyapps')
shinyapps::setAccountInfo(xxxxx)
library(shinyapps)
Then I run the following code:

install.packages("shiny")
install.packages("dygraphs")
library(shiny)
library(dygraphs)
library(xts)

####USER INTERFACE####
ui <- fluidPage(
  #Daily unemployment
  dateRangeInput("daterange", "Select Date Range", start = "2015-06-01", end = "2015-06-30", min = NULL, max = NULL, format = "yyyy-mm-dd", startview = "month", weekstart = 0, language = "en", separator = " to "),
  dygraphOutput("resupdatets", width="100%", height = "400px"),

  #For Date of Update, days of unemployment
  dateInput("updatedate", "Select Date", value = "2015-06-01", min = "2015-06-01", max = "2015-06-30", format = "yyyy-mm-dd", startview = "month", weekstart = 0, language = "en"),
  dygraphOutput("duration", width="100%", height = "400px"),

  #Daily unemployment based on work experience
  dateRangeInput("daterangeworkexp", "Select Date Range", start = "2015-06-01", end = "2015-06-30", min = NULL, max = NULL, format = "yyyy-mm-dd", startview = "month", weekstart = 0, language = "en", separator = " to "),
  selectInput("selectworkexp", "Select Years of Work Experience", choices=list("All"="0", "Less than 1 year" = "1", "1 to 3 years" = "3", "4 to 6 years" = "6", "7 to 10 years"="10", "More than 10"= "11")),
  dygraphOutput("resupdateworkexp", width="100%", height = "400px")
  )

####SERVER####
server <- function(input, output) {
  #Daily unemployment
  output$resupdatets<-renderDygraph({
    selecteddates<-with(lastupdateemp, lastupdateemp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterange[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterange[2])),])
    count<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(selecteddates))[,1]*0+table(na.omit(selecteddates))[,2])
    count<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(count)), count[,1])
    colnames(count)<- c("Date", "Unemployed")
    count <- xts(count, order.by <http://order.by> = count$Date, unique = FALSE)
    dygraph(count, main = "Daily Unemployment", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
    })
  #For Date of Update, days of unemployment
  output$duration<-renderDygraph({
    selectedupdate<-with(zoomlastupdate, zoomlastupdate[(Lastupdate == as.Date(input$updatedate, '%Y-%m-%d')),])
    count1<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(selectedupdate))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(selectedupdate))[,2,1])
    count1<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(count1)), count1[,1])
    colnames(count1)<- c("Date", "Unemployed")
    count1 <- xts(count1, order.by <http://order.by> = count1$Date, unique = FALSE)
    dygraph(count1, main = "Unemployed Since", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
  })

  #Daily unemployment based on work experience
  output$resupdateworkexp<-renderDygraph({
    if (input$selectworkexp=="0"){
      selecteddates<-with(lastupdateworkexp, lastupdateworkexp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[2])),])
      x1<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years < 1),])
      countx1<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x1))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x1))[,2,1])
      countx1<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx1)), x1=countx1[,1])
      x3<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >= 1 & Years<=3),])
      countx3<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x3))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x3))[,2,1])
      countx3<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx3)), x3=countx3[,1])
      x6<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >= 4 & Years<=6),])
      countx6<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x6))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x6))[,2,1])
      countx6<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx6)), x6=countx6[,1])
      x10<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >= 7 & Years<=10),])
      countx10<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x10))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x10))[,2,1])
      countx10<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx10)), x10=countx10[,1])
      x11<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >10),])
      countx11<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x11))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x11))[,2,1])
      countx11<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx11)), x11=countx11[,1])
      xall<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(countx1$Date), "x1"=countx1$x1, "x3"=countx3$x3, "x6"=countx6$x6, "x10"=countx10$x10, "x11"=countx11$x11)

      countall <- xts(xall, order.by <http://order.by> = xall$Date, unique = FALSE)
      dygraph(countall, main = "Daily Unemployment (By Work Experience)", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dySeries("x1", label = "Less than 1 year", color="#0404B4") %>% dySeries("x3", label = "1 to 3 years", color="#1C1C1C") %>% dySeries("x6", label = "3 to 6 years", color="#FF0000") %>% dySeries("x10", label = "7 to 10 years", color="#6A0888") %>% dySeries("x11", label = "Above 10 years", color="#01A9DB") %>% dyLegend(width=700,show="onmouseover") %>% dyHighlight(highlightCircleSize = 3, highlightSeriesBackgroundAlpha = 0.5, hideOnMouseOut = FALSE)
      }
    else if (input$selectworkexp=="1"){
    selecteddates<-with(lastupdateworkexp, lastupdateworkexp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[2])),])
    x1<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years < 1),])
    countx1<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x1))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x1))[,2,1])
    countx1<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx1)), x1=countx1[,1])
    countx1 <- xts(countx1, order.by <http://order.by> = countx1$Date, unique = FALSE)
    dygraph(countx1, main = "Daily Unemployment (Work Experience: Less than 1 Year)", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dySeries("x1", label = "Unemployed", color="#0404B4") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
    }
    else if (input$selectworkexp=="3"){
      selecteddates<-with(lastupdateworkexp, lastupdateworkexp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[2])),])
      x3<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >= 1 & Years<=3),])
      countx3<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x3))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x3))[,2,1])
      countx3<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx3)), x3=countx3[,1])
      countx3 <- xts(countx3, order.by <http://order.by> = countx3$Date, unique = FALSE)
      dygraph(countx3, main = "Daily Unemployment (Work Experience: 1 to 3 Years)", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dySeries("x3", label = "Unemployed", color="#1C1C1C") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
    }
    else if (input$selectworkexp=="6"){
      selecteddates<-with(lastupdateworkexp, lastupdateworkexp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[2])),])
      x6<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >= 4 & Years<=6),])
      countx6<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x6))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x6))[,2,1])
      countx6<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx6)), x6=countx6[,1])
      countx6 <- xts(countx6, order.by <http://order.by> = countx6$Date, unique = FALSE)
      dygraph(countx6, main = "Daily Unemployment (Work Experience: 4 to 6 Years)", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dySeries("x6", label = "Unemployed", color="#FF0000") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
    }
    else if (input$selectworkexp=="10"){
      selecteddates<-with(lastupdateworkexp, lastupdateworkexp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[2])),])
      x10<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >= 7 & Years<=10),])
      countx10<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x10))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x10))[,2,1])
      countx10<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx10)), x10=countx10[,1])
      countx10 <- xts(countx10, order.by <http://order.by> = countx10$Date, unique = FALSE)
      dygraph(countx10, main = "Daily Unemployment (Work Experience: 7 to 10 Years)", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dySeries("x10", label = "Unemployed", color="#6A0888") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
    }
    else if (input$selectworkexp=="11"){
      selecteddates<-with(lastupdateworkexp, lastupdateworkexp[(lastupdate >= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[1]) & lastupdate <= as.Date(input$daterangeworkexp[2])),])
      x11<-with(selecteddates, selecteddates[(Years >10),])
      countx11<- as.data.frame(table(na.omit(x11))[,1,1]*0+table(na.omit(x11))[,2,1])
      countx11<- data.frame(Date=as.Date(rownames(countx11)), x11=countx11[,1])
      countx11 <- xts(countx11, order.by <http://order.by> = countx11$Date, unique = FALSE)
      dygraph(countx11, main = "Daily Unemployment (Work Experience: Above 10 Years)", xlab="Date", ylab="Number of Unemployed Persons") %>% dySeries("x11", label = "Unemployed", color="#01A9DB") %>% dyLegend(show="onmouseover")
    }

    })

}

messages.body_plain:
The instructions are in the link that was sent, here is the relevant portion

https://www.rstudio.com/products/shinyapps-io-authentication-authorization/#Migrating

On your local system, rename the passwords.txt file in /shinyapps to old_passwords.txt.
Re-deploy your application using shinyapps::deployApp()

messages.body_plain:
Abigail,
I would recommend you try out some of the following:

- Break out your ui, and your server portions into a ui.R and server.R files
- Take out any install.packages() in your .R files because the shinyapps package will take care of detecting which versions of those packages and will install them on the server automatically.

I think if you want to go with the single page application, you may want to rename your file to shiny.R, but I haven't tried that myself.  It sounds like that is what the message is indicating in the error message you are receiving.

Best,
Tareef

Hwanwoo,
I am sorry we seem to be talking past each other.  If you want to have a private application, you will have to go to the standard paid plan.  We have NO private applications in the free plan.

It sounds like what you are looking for is a private application on our free plan, which we don't support now that we are out of the beta period.

If you don't mind your application being public, you can skip the first step in the instructions, and simply make the changes that are outlined and you can deploy again.  This will allow you to stay on a free plan and to get access to your application once again.

-Tareef

> > Andy - thanks for such a thoughtful response. I do agree with you on all the issues and that most of the solutions are not ideal, and arbitrary cutoffs are bad, etc.  I do like the last idea of adding a special field in DESCRIPTION for shinyapps, maybe that idea can be explored more in depth to see if it makes sense.
> >
> >
> > On Thursday, 2 July 2015 08:41:48 UTC-7, Andy Kipp wrote:
> > > Dean et al.,
> > >
> > > When shinyapps does dependency detection on an app, it does not include suggested packages. The reason for this is that dependency detection is recursive, and when we did our initial testing of including suggested packages, even relatively simple applications ended up having hundreds of dependencies. Additionally, many times suggested packages are suggested because they are burdensome to install or have non-trivial system dependancies which may or may not work on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
> > >
> > > However, this is not to say that our current approach is ideal for exactly the reasons you've outlined. We could look at some alternate approaches. Some ideas:
> > >
> > > 1) Right now our dependency detection code is unsophisticated in that it requires that all detected dependencies (e.g. Depends, Imports, LinkingTo) be installed. Including suggested packages results in the explosion of packages I mentioned above.
> > >
> > > An alternate approach may be to only include suggested packages if they are actually installed on the end-user's system. For example: if an app depends on shinyjs and V8 is suggested by shinyjs, if the user has the V8 package installed locally we will include it (and its recursive dependencies). Conversely, if the package rJava was suggested, but not installed locally we wont include it.
> > >
> > > This approach may or not be better for a number of reasons. I did some testing and in my opinion we still end up with lots of packages still being installed unnecessarily (many user's end up with lots of packages installed on their system over time, and packages often have many suggested packages that are not really related).

> > > > Dean et al.,

> > > > When shinyapps does dependency detection on an app, it does not include suggested packages. The reason for this is that dependency detection is recursive, and when we did our initial testing of including suggested packages, even relatively simple applications ended up having hundreds of dependencies. Additionally, many times suggested packages are suggested because they are burdensome to install or have non-trivial system dependancies which may or may not work on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.
> > > >
> > > > However, this is not to say that our current approach is ideal for exactly the reasons you've outlined. We could look at some alternate approaches. Some ideas:
> > > >
> > > > 1) Right now our dependency detection code is unsophisticated in that it requires that all detected dependencies (e.g. Depends, Imports, LinkingTo) be installed. Including suggested packages results in the explosion of packages I mentioned above.
> > > >
> > > > An alternate approach may be to only include suggested packages if they are actually installed on the end-user's system. For example: if an app depends on shinyjs and V8 is suggested by shinyjs, if the user has the V8 package installed locally we will include it (and its recursive dependencies). Conversely, if the package rJava was suggested, but not installed locally we wont include it.
> > > >
> > > > This approach may or not be better for a number of reasons. > > > > 36     labeling     0.2
> > > > 37   colorspace   1.2-4
> > > >
> > > > Which is a little better, but 37 vs 12 is a lot. The reason for this is because shiny has 6 suggested dependencies, which themselves have lots of required dependencies (again this is for the simplest possible app).
> > > >
> > > > This might be workable, but the distinction seems arbitrary in my mind. I like to avoid arbitrary distinctions as they tend to lead to more confusion in the end.
> > > >
> > > > So my feeling is that this approach sounds great in theory, but in practice its still too many packages to install. Perhaps this option can be toggle-able via an option. But I feel like this may be useless in the end, because it still requires the end-user to know they need to set the option. In my experience nobody ever RTFM, so this is probably no better then documenting that the end user needs to do require(XXX) for suggested packages in their app when running on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io/>, as it still requires the user to do something.
> > > >
> > > > You can checkout my code for this test here: https://github.com/rstudio/rsconnect/compare/suggested-package-dependencies?expand=1
> > > >
> > > > 2) Another possibility is to allow package maintainers to use a special DESCRIPTION field to have custom dependencies for shinyapps:
> > > >
> > > > For example we could look for a ShinyAppsDepends field in the DESCRIPTION file for a package:
> > > >
> > > > ShinyAppsDepends: V8
> > > >
> > > > If we see that, we can include it. This approach might be better, because only package maintainers would have to know about the workaround, rather then end-users.
> > > >
> > > > Anyway, these are some ideas, and I am open to other suggestions as well.
> > > >
> > > > -Andy
> > > >

messages.subject: How to make time sensitive app work
messages.subject_clean: How to make time sensitive app work
messages.body_plain:
Dear group,

I have built an app that is time-sensitive, meaning that its output changes depending on some values. It's essentially a game with sequential rounds. In server.R I calculate the difference between Sys.time() and the begin time (which I set manually). This difference is transformed into a value "n", which denotes which output to load. This solution fails on some occassions and it is not entirely clear to me why. If I use refresh after sufficient time elapsed for a new round, Shiny never produces the correct "n". If I close the app and load it again then most of times it produces the correct "n", but sometimes it does not. If I check the log in case of failures then it looks like shiny is not running the calculation for "n". I am assuming this has something to do with closing previous sessions. But I am not sure how to proceed from here, and make the timing work in the app. Any ideas on this would be very welcome.

All the best,

Gijs

messages.subject: iframe making all referral traffic disappear for Google Analytics
messages.subject_clean: iframe making all referral traffic disappear for Google Analytics
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

One thing you may not be aware of since the iframe move, is how it affects tracking tags.

I put Google Tag Manager including Google Analytics on my apps, but since the iframe move all referral data (where people click to visit the app) is destroyed, as the iframe can't pass it through to the GTM tag within. It now all shows up as direct traffic.

I'm not sure what could be done without you offering custom support for GA tags, but if you do then you could perhaps have a field to insert the tracking tag on the parent frame (which will then be able to track the inner frame via cross domain tracking), or pass the referrer info somehow into the iframe in the session object.

Yours sincerely,
Mark

The tutorial will take you a couple of hours to get through, you could also watch a three part webinar we have posted here <https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/> that will walk you through how Shiny works.  You don't really knit a shiny application.  You can run it by typing runApp() in the directory that has your app.R or your ui.R and server.R files.

The discussion list that you will find particularly helpful for asking shiny related questions is the shiny-discuss list <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/shiny-discuss> which provides support for what shiny is and how to use it.  shinyapps-users is a discussion list that is focused on helping people who are trying to deploy their shiny applications to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> cloud.

messages.subject: How to update SelectInput (in renderUI) dependent on SliderInput using actionButton
messages.subject_clean: How to update SelectInput (in renderUI) dependent on SliderInput using actionButton
messages.body_plain:
I'm working on an app for conjoint analysis - client is seting the offers and he gets the results. Client can change the offerts remotly (simply using widgets) or import the CSV file with all values and set them up clicking **actionButton**. Problem is that some wigets are dependent from another (I'm using **renderUI** for those dependent widgets) and **update** functions in **observeEvent** are not working for them.

I'll explain more precisely in this simple example:

Here I've got 2 offerts with 2 wigets each: 'cost' and 'type'. When cost is greater than 89.99  we can choose '1 SIM' or 'Family' offert type, otherwise there is only '1 SIM' type. When I'm using **actionButton** the **updateSliderInput** is changing the 'cost' value, but 'type' value is still the same. I was trying with two **observeEvent** with different priorities (one for 'cost', one for 'type') but it wasn't working too.

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(
  column(12,
         tabsetPanel(id="xyz",
                     tabPanel("Offers",
                              fluidRow(
                                column(2,
                                       sliderInput("cost1", label = "Cost",
                                                   min =39.99 , max =189.99 , value =49.99,step=0.01,post=" zł"),
                                       uiOutput("select1a")),

messages.body_plain:
That make sense now that I think about it (same origin policy).

I think this should be possible to make work. My understanding of what your trying to do is generate a URL with a session identifier and redirect the user to that URL.

I think what is happening is that inside the iframe, the location is the internal URL (which is used by shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> for internal purposes). When you modify that location using location.pathname.replace, the parent iframe detects that new URL is a URL that is outside the app (since it doesn't match the top frame URL) and it basically intercepts this and removes the iframe (like if you had a link to some other URL inside your app, the iframe get's removed automatically).

The trick here I think is to generate a URL using the top frame URL, but still change the current iframe's location.

So I think what you need to do here is:

var oldpath = window.parent.location.pathname;
var newpath = oldpath.replace(/\/_w_(\w+)/, "");
var path = location.pathname = newpath;

I have not tested this, but I think it should put you the right track.

-Andy

On Friday, July 24, 2015 at 5:47:21 AM UTC-7, Andy Kipp wrote:
> That make sense now that I think about it (same origin policy).
>
> I think this should be possible to make work. My understanding of what your trying to do is generate a URL with a session identifier and redirect the user to that URL.
>
> I think what is happening is that inside the iframe, the location is the internal URL (which is used by shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> for internal purposes). When you modify that location using location.pathname.replace, the parent iframe detects that new URL is a URL that is outside the app (since it doesn't match the top frame URL) and it basically intercepts this and removes the iframe (like if you had a link to some other URL inside your app, the iframe get's removed automatically).
>
> The trick here I think is to generate a URL using the top frame URL, but still change the current iframe's location.
>
> So I think what you need to do here is:
>
> var oldpath = window.parent.location.pathname;
> var newpath = oldpath.replace(/\/_w_(\w+)/, "");
> var path = location.pathname = newpath;
>
> I have not tested this, but I think it should put you the right track.
>
> -Andy

messages.subject: deployApp but for an app that is not in a file
messages.subject_clean: deployApp but for an app that is not in a file
messages.body_plain:
I know this may seem odd, but supposing, instead of writing out the app and sticking it in an R file, one basically constructs the app within R. See the code below for an example of what I am talking about

the_server <- function(the_input, the_output) {
the_output$visual <- renderPlot(SOME PLOT THAT USES the_year AND the_metal as controls)
  }

the_ui <- fluidPage(
sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
radioButtons(\" the_year \",\" year:\",c(\" 2014\"=\" 2014\",\" \
2015\"=\" 2015\",\" 2016\"=\" 2016\")),
radioButtons(\" the_metal \",\" metal:\",c(\" Bronze \"=\" Bronze \",\
\" Silver \"=\" Silver \",\" Gold \"=\" Gold \",\" Platinum \"=\" \
Platinum \"))
    ),
    mainPanel(plotOutput(\" visual \"))
  )
)

sa<- shinyApp(ui=the_ui,server=the_server)

Now, at this point I could run print(sa) and a web browser would open and everything would work.

But suppose instead I want to deploy sa as a shinyapp so that it can run on others computers. The deployApp function appears to want a file name.  Is there a way to do this.

All help appreciated.

(By the way, this question emerges because I am trying to get Mathematica to produce Shiny Apps.  I've actually succeeded, but I now want to take it to the next step and let those apps be used by the public.)

Hi,

I suspect the issue is that your database is not accessible to the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers. If the database is hosted inside a corporate or campus network, you will likely need to contact your network administrators so your firewall can be configured to allow access from shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers.

The ip addresses for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> servers, can be found here <https://www.rstudio.com/faq-items/how-do-i-give-access-to-my-rds-instance-for-an-application-i-have-deployed-on-shinyapps-io/>.

-Andy

messages.subject: How much can shinyapps upload? Warning in run(timeoutMs)
messages.subject_clean: How much can shinyapps upload? Warning in run(timeoutMs)
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

My app first uploads a .R file from a public dropbox folder, and it uses the values in that .R file to run the app. The code is (both in server.R and ui.R):

url <- "https://[mypublicdropboxfolder]/file.RData"
repmis::source_data(url)

This works fine for the first few iterations of the app, but eventually crashes. It gives this warning: Warning in run(timeoutMs) and announces that it cannot find some values it needs to run the app.

I am wondering whether the file that is uploaded is too large (it's only 43.6 kb)? Or whether the method to upload is too slow (any other ideas?). Or whether there is some other explanation for this error?

I already set my app size to xx large. But that didn't change anything.

Any help would be very welcome.

All the best,

Gijs

messages.subject_clean: Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 61153167 error: Unhandled Exception: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'is_directed'
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am very new using shiny, so I apologize in advance for my ignorance. I want to upload a really simple app to my shiniapps.io <http://shiniapps.io> page for my collaborator to check the data easily. However, I can't seem to find a way to address this error message:

Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 61153167 error: Unhandled Exception: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'is_directed'

Any clues or advice are more than welcome. This is my entire code:

#install.packages('devtools')
#install.packages('shiny')
#install.packages('rmarkdown')
#devtools::install_github('rstudio/shinyapps')

library(shinyapps)
library(d3heatmap)
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  h1("Influenza Infection in NK Cells. RNA-Seq data"),
  selectInput("palette", "Palette", c("YlOrRd", "RdYlBu", "Greens", "Blues")),
  checkboxInput("cluster", "Apply clustering"),
  d3heatmapOutput("heatmap")
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$heatmap <- renderD3heatmap({
    d3heatmap(
      scale(heatmap_matrix),
      colors = input$palette,
      dendrogram = if (input$cluster) "both" else "none"
    )
  })
}

app_shiny <- shinyApp(ui, server)
save(app_shiny,file="App_heatmap.html")

shinyapps::deployApp('App_heatmap.html')

Thank you so much!

Marta
